chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:
"When you see the crescent, then break your fast, or if a just Muslim bears witness to it,
and if you do not see the crescent except from the middle of the day or its end, then: "complete the fasting until the night."
So if it is obscured from you, then count thirty nights, then break your fast."

key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: nightfall, the time until which the fast must be completed
key_terms.الْهِلَالَ: the new crescent moon by which the month’s end is determined
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ: the completion of the month as thirty days/nights
key_terms.غُمَّ: was obscured or hidden from sight
key_terms.فَأَفْطِرُوا: break the fast at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: How is the end of Ramadan established according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for ending the fast based on sighting the crescent of Shawwal or the testimony of a just Muslim. If the crescent is only seen during the day, the fast must be completed until night, and if visibility is obscured, the month is completed as thirty nights.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1911 - In the narration of Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (as), who said that Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), said:
"When you see the crescent, break your fast, or if a trustworthy Muslim testifies to seeing it, then break your fast.
If you do not see the crescent except in the middle or the end of the day, then 'complete your fast until night.'
If the crescent is obscured from you, count thirty nights and then break your fast."
